speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I see you are presenting with shortness of breath, increased abdominal girth, and a large ovarian mass. To determine the underlying cause, have you experienced any unintentional weight loss or changes in bowel habits like constipation or bloating?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old nulliparous woman. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath and noticeable increase in abdominal size over the past month. She denies any significant medical history, previous surgeries, or use of medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. Given your age and the ovarian mass, have you noticed any abnormal vaginal bleeding or pelvic pain, and what are the current results of your serum CA-125 level? REQUEST TEST: CA-125

speaker: Doctor
text: The CA-125 level is normal, which is helpful. Given the large ovarian mass and shortness of breath, could you describe the nature of the breathlessness—is it worse when lying flat, or do you have any cough or chest pain? REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest_Abdomen_Pelvis

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT Chest/Abdomen/Pelvis Findings: Large heterogeneous mass in the right ovary with associated peritoneal carcinomatosis. Significant right-sided pleural effusion present. Ascites noted. No evidence of lung parenchymal consolidation or pneumothorax.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Ovarian Cancer with malignant ascites and pleural effusion (Malignant Pericardial/Mediastinal Effusion).
